source_text:
καταριθμεῖ. καὶ ἀριθμήσας τὸν ἐκ τούτων τῶν μελῶν συνεστῶτα ἄνθρωπον,
παρακελεύεται ἀπεκδύσασθαι τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον σὺν ταῖς πράξεσιν αὐτοῦ· ὥστε
ὁ παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπός ἐστι τὸ φρόνημα τὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, μέλη δὲ αὐτοῦ αἱ πράξεις τῶν
ἁμαρτημάτων. καὶ ὥσπερ ἐστὶ παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος, οὕτως ἐστὶ καὶ νέος τοῦτ' ἔστι τὸ
φρόνημα τὸ πνευματικόν· καὶ μέλη αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀγαθαὶ πράξεις, ὡς καὶ ἀριθμεῖ λέγων
χρηστότητα, μακροθυμίαν καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Kol3,11 Τοῦτο ὅμοιόν ἐστι τῷ ἵνα ᾖ τὰ πάντα
ἐν πᾶσιν. ὃ δέ φησιν τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· ἵνα ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς φρονοῦσι τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ πάντα
ὁ θεὸς ἐνεργῇ. ὅταν γὰρ τὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ φρονῇς καὶ ποιῇς, αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν διὰ
σοῦ καὶ ἔστιν ἐν σοί. Ὅμοιόν ἐστιν· ἵνα ᾖ ὁ θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν· οὐκ οὐρανὸς ἐν
οὐρανῷ, οὐδὲ γῆ ἐν γῇ. ἀλλ' ὅ φησιν τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· ὅταν τὰ τούτου φρονῇς καὶ
ποιῇς, θεός ἐστιν ὁ ποιῶν διὰ σοῦ, καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν σοὶ τῷ ποιεῖν σε ἃ ἐκείνῳ
δοκεῖ. 328 Kol 3,14 Ἀγάπης μὴ προηγουμένης οὐδὲν τῶν δεόντων τελειοῦται· τότε
γὰρ καὶ τοῦ κακῶς ποιεῖν ἀλλήλους ἀπεχόμεθα καὶ τοῦ εὖ ποιεῖν φροντίζομεν, ὅταν
ἀλλήλους ἀγαπῶμεν. Kol 3,15 Μὴ οἱ πλανῶντες ὑμᾶς, φησί, καταβραβευέτωσαν,
ἀλλ' ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Χριστοῦ βραβευέτω ἐν ὑμῖν εἰς τὸ ἡνῶσθαι Χριστῷ· καὶ εὐχάριστοι
γίνεσθε. τίνι; δηλονότι τῷ καλέσαντι ὑμᾶς Χριστῷ, καὶ μὴ ἀγγέλοις ὑποτρέχητε. Μὴ
οἱ πλανῶντες καταβραβευέτωσαν, ἀλλ' ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Χριστοῦ βραβευέτω ἐν ταῖς
καρδίαις ὑμῶν, τοῦτ' ἔστι τῷ ἡνῶσθαι Χριστῷ καὶ τὰ αὐτοῦ φρονεῖν. εἶτα πάλιν
προτροπή. Kol 4,1 Τῶν δούλων ὑμῖν, φησί, μετ' εὐνοίας ὑπηρετούντων, καὶ ὑμεῖς οἱ
δεσπόται κατὰ τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὸ ἶσον αὐτοὺς ἀμείβεσθε ἐν τῇ προσηκούσῃ
κηδεμονίᾳ. τὴν ἰσότητα οὖν κατὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν.
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing the second form of the Colossians 3:5 / 3:9-10 notes] ... he lists. And having numbered the man made up of these members, he urges them to strip off the old man with his deeds; so the old man is the mind-set of sin, and his members the deeds of the sins. And just as there is an old man, so there is also a new one, that is, the spiritual mind-set; and his members are the good deeds, as he also numbers them, saying kindness, long-suffering and the rest.
Colossians 3:11. This is like "that he may be all things in all." What he says is this: that in all who think the things of God, God may work all things. For when you think and do the things of Christ, he is the one doing (them) through you, and he is in you.
[Second form, unmarked repetition:] It is like: "that God may be all things in all"; not heaven in heaven, nor earth in earth. But what he says is this: when you think and do the things of this one, God is the one doing through you, and he himself is in you by your doing what seems good to him.
Colossians 3:14. Love not going first, nothing of what is needed is perfected; for then we both keep from doing harm to one another and take thought for doing good, when we love one another.
Colossians 3:15. Let not those who mislead you, he says, rob you of the prize, but let the peace of Christ be umpire among you for being united to Christ; "and be thankful." To whom? Clearly to Christ who called you; and do not run for shelter to angels.
[Second form, unmarked repetition:] Let not those who mislead rob of the prize, but let the peace of Christ be umpire in your hearts, that is, by being united to Christ and thinking his things. Then again an exhortation.
Colossians 4:1. Since your slaves, he says, serve with goodwill, you too, the masters, repay them according to what is just and equal with fitting care. So the equality (is) according to the goodwill.
pass_b_english: … members. And having listed the man made up of these members, he urges them to strip off the old man with his deeds. … As there is an old man, so there is a new one too, that is, the spiritual mind; and its members are good deeds, which he also lists when he says “kindness, long-suffering” and the rest (Colossians 3:12).

On Colossians 3:11: This is like the words “that he may be all in all” (1 Corinthians 15:28). What he means is this: that God may work all things in all who set their minds on the things of God. When you think and do what belongs to Christ, he is the one acting through you, and he is in you.
The second catena form adds: … not heaven in heaven, nor earth in earth. … He is in you by your doing what pleases him.

On Colossians 3:14: Unless love leads the way, none of our duties is carried through to completion. It is when we love one another that we both keep from harming one another and take care to do one another good.

On Colossians 3:15: Do not let those who lead you astray, he says, rob you of the prize; let the peace of Christ be the umpire among you, so that you are united to Christ. “And be thankful.” To whom? To Christ, of course, who called you; and do not run to angels for shelter.
The second catena form adds: … in your hearts, that is, by being united to Christ and setting your minds on what is his. Then comes another exhortation.
On Colossians 4:1: Since your slaves, he says, serve you with goodwill, you masters must also repay them justly and fairly, with the care that is fitting. So fairness answers to their goodwill.

choices.term: καταριθμεῖ. καὶ ἀριθμήσας … χρηστότητα, μακροθυμίαν καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς.
choices.english: second form of the 3:5 / 3:9–10 notes, printed only where it adds
choices.why: Continues the unmarked repetition begun at the end of u02-rem-mid. Kept: 'having listed the man made of these members, he urges them to strip off the old man with his deeds' and 'its members are good deeds, which he lists: kindness, long-suffering'. Dropped as repeats: 'the old man is the mind-set of sin, its members the deeds of sin' and the 'new man = spiritual mind' clause (kept only as needed for the sentence).
rejected: printing the whole second form (old paragraph 1)

choices.term: Τοῦτο ὅμοιόν ἐστι τῷ ἵνα ᾖ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν
choices.english: This is like the words “that he may be all in all” (1 Corinthians 15:28).
choices.why: The quoted words are 1 Corinthians 15:28 ('that God may be all in all'); the old English printed '(Col 3:11)' after them (SOURCE_ISSUES item 2) and a bare 'Col 3:11' label in the paragraph (item 3).

choices.term: Ὅμοιόν ἐστιν· ἵνα ᾖ ὁ θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν … ἃ ἐκείνῳ δοκεῖ.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed (Colossians 3:11): reduced to 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Unmarked repetition. Added material kept: 'not heaven in heaven, nor earth in earth' and 'he is in you by your doing what pleases him'.

choices.term: Μὴ οἱ πλανῶντες καταβραβευέτωσαν, ἀλλ' ἡ εἰρήνη … εἶτα πάλιν προτροπή.
choices.english: Doublet collapsed (Colossians 3:15): reduced to 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: The old English printed the sentence 'Let not those who mislead ... be awarded' twice in one paragraph (SOURCE_ISSUES item 1). Added material kept: 'in your hearts', 'setting your minds on what is his', 'then comes another exhortation'.
καταβραβεύω = decide against, deprive of the prize (Colossians 2:18 vocabulary); old 'be awarded' reversed it.
Old English printed bare 'Col 3:11', 'Col 3:14', 'Col 3:15', 'Col 4:1' in mid-paragraph (SOURCE_ISSUES item 3); each now opens its own note.

choices.term: τὴν ἰσότητα οὖν κατὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν
choices.english: So fairness answers to their goodwill.
choices.why: Verbless phrase: the masters' 'equality' (4:1) is measured by the slaves' goodwill.
